clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter moving the family across the country in March 1952 and buying the apple orchard, within the year: June's homesickness and daily letters to her sister, her distance from Walter as he worked long hours, Glen's fights at school, Walter's cutoff from his brother Harlan over their father's land money, June's weeks in bed that first winter, rows between Walter and June over money for new trees, and June's anxiety easing as she joined the church choir by September 1953. These shifts in the extended family pile up from the move through the first winter and settle as June found her footing in the valley.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around Walter's orchard failing in May 1968 when the late frost took the whole crop and the bank called in the loan, within sixteen months: Walter's heavy drinking, his conflict with Glen over who was to blame, Glen's overfunctioning as he took over the family's money and talks with the bank, Glen's son Carl's asthma attacks worsening, Nora's bed-wetting, Ida's heart trouble found, and Walter's functioning rising as he stopped drinking in October 1969 and took work pruning trees. The shifts in the family settle as Walter stepped back from the loss and found work.

clusters.name: Glen's job lost, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen losing his job in February 1975 when the Ridgeport cannery closed, within fourteen months: Glen's functioning falling as he sat in the truck for hours, loud fights with Marian over money, Marian's overfunctioning as she took a second job at night, Nora's weight loss and stopped eating through the summer, Nora's distance from Marian as she kept to her room, and Nora's functioning rising by June 1976 as she began eating and made the track team. Glen's job beginning at the feed store in March 1976 marks the turn. Every shift in these months is within Nora's household, and no one else's shows then.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into the house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma moving into Nora and Sam's house in January 1990, within seventeen months: Nora's conflict with Wilma over the children's bedtimes and meals, Nora's distance from Sam as he worked late and kept out of the rows, Sam's move toward his mother, Owen's tantrums at preschool, Wilma's overfunctioning as she took over Lily's care, Nora's eczema flaring on both hands, Nora's conflict with Sam most nights through the fall, and Nora's eczema clearing over the summer of 1991. Wilma's move to a flat in town in June 1991 marks where the shifts settle.
